options.content:
# Auth Container Drilldown

Description of component and a list of all infrastructure.

Links to infra specific dashboards for another drilldown.

[Auth Container RDS](https://www.aws.com)

[Auth Container EKS](https://www.aws.com)

[Auth Container MSK](https://www.aws.com)

panels.description:
DataSource: elasticSearch; index: authgateway*

Condition: event.status:"SUCCESS"

Description: if the graph is going down, then the successful transactions are lowered, which implies the availability of the application. The red line indicates the expected baseline value. Click on the panel for application drilldown.
panels.title: Availability

panels.description:
DataSource: elasticSearch; index: authgateway*

Condition: Average "source.measurements.timeTaken"

Description: Query is reading the events for all transactionID and requestedURI of applications starting with auth*, so if the latency of one or more requestedURI's are increasing, it would effect the auth application health. Click on the panel for drill down.
panels.title: Latency

panels.description:
DataSource: elasticSearch; index: authgateway*

Condition: Count of 'event.application.keyword:auth*"

Description: the decline trend of the traffic line graph indicates that traffic is reached to selected application. Few areas you might need to troubleshoot is to
1. Check if Kafka consumer is broken.
2. Check if data write to Kafaka topic is still happening
3. Check if the traffic is reaching to selected application from upstream layer. To know the upstream layer, please refer to the architecture diagram panel or the documentation section in this dashboard.
panels.title: Traffic

panels.description:
DataSource: elasticSearch; index: authgateway*

Condition:  NOT source.responseCode:200

Description: Increase in the error rate will impacts the availability of the selected application, in this panel you'll see the trend of different statusCodes (i.e., 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx) based on the type of statusCode one can come to a a fair estimation on how to investigate
Ex: More 4xx implies the unauthorized or not resource not found error; 5xx implies issue at client side/server side. Click on the dashboard to navigate to drill down dashboard.
panels.title: Errors

panels.description:
Source: elasticSearch; Index: authgateway*

Condition: timeTaken >= 100 ms (source.requestedURI)

Description: When the application is facing high latency issues ( if the line graph in the latency panel under Overview section) is going high, then there could be few reasons for that behavior like network/connectivity b/w services, the payload of the data at the transit might be heavy, request processing time at server side could be high. One of the services/requested URI cloud be having high response time. This panel will give us the top 10 bad performing requestedURI for a selected application.

Click on the Transaction Level DrillDown link for see historical trend of the requested URI.
panels.title: Top Bad Performing URIs by ResponseTime

panels.description:
Source: elasticSearch; Index: authgateway*

Condition: responseCode != 200 (source.requestedURI)

Description: There could be few possible reasons when the application Availability is going down, it could be due to the connectivity to other micro service or dependent cloud services like s3/lambda/DB's etc., This panel will highlights the error count for requested URIs'. Click on Transaction Level Drilldown dashboard to see the trends over time for selected requestedURI.
panels.title: Top Bad Performing URIs by Error Count

Description: Evaluation of success rate is based on the combination of Cluster and container_name, the number on panel will show different colors based on the value. panels.description:
Datasource: Thanos

Measurement: jvm_gc_live_data_size_bytes; jvm_gc_live_data_size_bytes Condition: Max

Inputs; cluster, container_name

Description: Garbage collection can impact the performance of Java applications in unpredictable ways. When there is frequent GC activity, it adds a lot of CPU load and slows down application processing. In turn, this leads to slow execution of business transactions and ultimately affects the user experience of end-users accessing the Java application.
Excessive garbage collection activity can occur due to a memory leak in the Java application. Insufficient memory allocation to the JVM can also result in increased garbage collection activity. And when excessive garbage collection activity happens, it often manifests as increased CPU usage of the JVM!
panels.title: JVM GC data size(MB) live vs max

panels.description:
Datasource: Thanos

Measurements: jvm_gc_pause_seconds_count; Condition: Max

Inputs: cluster, contaner_name

Description: A garbage collection pause, also known as a stop-the-world event, happens when a region of memory is full and the JVM requires space to continue. During a pause all operations are suspended. Because a pause affects networking, the node can appear as down to other nodes in the cluster
panels.title: JVM GC pause(sec) by container

panels.description:
Datasource: Thanos

Measurement: jvm_buffer_count_buffers, jvm_buffer_memory_used_bytes, jvm_buffer_total_capacity_bytes; Condition: Max

Inputs: cluster, container_name

Description: Direct buffer memory is allocated outside the Java heap. It represents the operating system's native memory used by the JVM process.

Because direct buffers aren't freed up by the Garbage Collector, their impact on the memory footprint of an application might not be obvious. Therefore, direct buffers should be allocated primarily to large buffers that are used in the I/O operations.

https://docs.oracle.com/javase/8/docs/api/java/nio/Buffer.html
panels.title: JVM buffer count vs memory used vs total capacity (GB)

Inputs: cluster, container_name

Description: Class loaders are responsible for loading Java classes dynamically to the JVM (Java Virtual Machine) during runtime. They're also part of the JRE.
panels.title: JVM classes loaded vs unloaded

Description: Pod restarts is not a good sign of an app. There could be several reasons for pod restarts. A restarting container can indicate problems with memory (see the Out of Memory section), cpu usage, or just an application exiting prematurely. If a container is being restarted because of CPU usage, try increasing the requested and limit amounts for CPU in the pod spec

targets.expr: label_join((histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(istio_request_duration_milliseconds_bucket{reporter="destination"}[3m])) by (le, destination_workload, destination_workload_namespace)) / 1000) or histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(istio_request_duration_seconds_bucket{reporter="destination"}[3m])) by (le, destination_workload, destination_workload_namespace)), "destination_workload_var", ".", "destination_workload", "destination_workload_namespace")
